title: MessagesStore trusts caller id: overwrite and id-space DoS
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (MessagesStore::post_inbox)

Caller-supplied id is used as the stored key with no uniqueness check:

- Duplicate id overwrites sent HashMap entry, leaves sent_order unchanged, and appends a second inbox row. Spec 18.1.1 says id is a unique message ID.
- id = u64::MAX sets next_id to u64::MAX+1, so later auto-assigned POSTs return 5.03 Service Unavailable while explicit ids still succeed. One untrusted POST can exhaust the id space.

Python MessagesResource has the same next_id = max(next_id, id+1) behavior. Spec is the arbiter: ids are unique, and 5.03 is for id-space exhaustion after legitimate assign, not a client-chosen latch.

Fix: reject (4.00) an id that already exists; do not advance next_id past the next unused value based on an untrusted id, or treat caller id as a hint only.

Perspectives: security, correctness.
close_reason: Reject duplicate caller ids with 4.00 (no sent overwrite, no extra inbox row). Do not latch next_id from untrusted ids, so id=u64::MAX cannot exhaust auto-assign. Tests: duplicate reject, MAX latch, skip occupied. cargo test -p lichen-client --lib msg + messaging_vectors + receipt_vectors; clippy -D warnings clean.
